summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with metastatic cholangiocarcinoma on surveillance and a history of recurrent cholangitis due to multidrug-resistant E. coli, was admitted with fever and nausea. He had recently completed a four-week course of IV antibiotics for a hepatic abscess but had inadvertently stopped apixaban and ursodiol. On admission, he was restarted on ceftazidime-avibactam and metronidazole. MRI revealed new subcentimeter liver microabscesses. A multidisciplinary team decided to place a percutaneous transhepatic biliary drain to improve biliary drainage and prevent recurrence. A PICC line was placed for IV antibiotic administration. He was discharged home on a four-week course of IV and oral antibiotics, with plans for follow-up MRI and clinic visit. His portal vein thrombosis was managed with apixaban, and iron deficiency anemia was addressed with IV iron infusions.
